title: Riots Erupt in Buenos Aires After Argentina's World Cup Final Loss to Spain
excerpt: Police fired tear gas and rubber bullets after thousands of fans clashed with officers near the Obelisk following Spain's extra-time victory.
body:
• At least 15 people were arrested and several civilians and police officers injured in Buenos Aires after Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain in extra time.
  • Fans near the Obelisk monument threw glass bottles at police, who responded with tear gas, water cannons, and rubber bullets in clashes lasting 20 minutes.
  • The on-pitch violence was equally stark — Argentina's Leandro Paredes was red-carded for punching Spain's Gavi after the final whistle.
  • The disorder caps a bitter tournament ending for Argentina, whose coach Lionel Scaloni has cast doubt on his own future with the team.

Riots swept through central Buenos Aires on Sunday night after Argentina fell to Spain in the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, a 1-0 extra-time defeat that ended the defending champions' bid to retain the trophy.

Thousands of fans had gathered around the Obelisk, the 67.5-meter national monument in the heart of the capital, to watch the match on large screens. When the final whistle confirmed Spain's victory — sealed by Ferran Torres's goal from a Nico Williams assist in the 113th minute — frustration spilled into violence.

Clashes at the Obelisk

According to Argentine newspaper Infobae, the disorder began at around 11:45 p.m. local time when several fans scaled the protective fence surrounding the Obelisk. Glass bottles and debris were hurled at police officers stationed nearby.

Officers responded with tear gas, water cannons, and rubber bullets in an attempt to contain the crowd. Seven police officers sustained injuries during the 20-minute confrontation, the outlet reported. Several civilians were also hurt, including a man kicked in the face during the melee and a woman who required medical attention.

Riot police armed with shields and batons advanced from Corrientes Avenue southward through the city, gradually dispersing the crowd. Images from the scene showed streets littered with broken glass and smoldering debris.

On-Pitch Brawl Mars the Final

The disorder on the streets mirrored ugly scenes inside MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where the match was played. After the final whistle, Argentina players lashed out at their Spanish opponents.

Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch at a Spanish substitute, while Leandro Paredes attacked Spain's Gavi, throwing multiple punches and slamming him to the ground. Referee Slavko Vincic showed Paredes a straight red card for the assault.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. There is no place or space for that. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina."

— Alan Shearer, BBC Sport analyst

Argentina had struggled across 120 minutes against a composed Spanish side. Spain controlled possession and created the sharper chances, with Williams — whose parents immigrated from Ghana to Spain — providing the crucial assist after his initial shot had been disallowed for an earlier foul.

Scaloni's Uncertain Future

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni, who guided the team to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar, appeared visibly shaken in his post-match press conference. He expressed doubt about continuing in the role, telling reporters he was unsure whether he would remain in charge.

For Lionel Messi, now 39, the final was widely expected to be his last World Cup appearance. The Argentine captain had described the match as "the last tango" in an emotional pre-game interview, adding a layer of poignancy to the defeat.

A Tournament That Captivated Millions

The World Cup final was the most-watched sporting event of 2026, with viewership records shattered across the globe. In India, where cricket dominates the sporting calendar, the tournament attracted significant attention — particularly the final's dramatic climax and the Paredes brawl, which trended across Indian social media within minutes of the final whistle.

Buenos Aires authorities said the situation was brought under control by early Monday morning. No fatalities were reported.
